what: Converts vertical scroll into horizontal travel of a wide image strip — the panel height is extended to strip width ÷ .6, the inner stage stays pinned to the screen, and the strip is pushed left by the progress. The strip gets a fresh .6s cubic.out quickTo every frame, so it approaches only along the head of the curve and follows stickily, and layers inside the strip (data-par) are pushed further by progress × par px, front (−) flowing fast and back (+) flowing slow. Progress is exported as --fx-progress — for timelines walking sideways through eras, picture villages and horizontal galleries

options.ratio: Panel height = Band width ÷ ratio, default .6 (smaller means the same distance scrolls longer)
options.dur: Curve length the band follows (seconds), default .6 — 0 attaches immediately

parts.stage: Stage that sticks to the screen — header band height set by --fx-top
parts.layer: Layer flowing separately inside the band — data-par="-600" Extra px pushed past the end when it goes all the way

use: …

from.where: index.js rendering() — moves .sec-slides by (strip width − window width) × progress with quickTo .6 cubic.out, each building floor 200px × (−5~7)

note: In the original, the height sits inside .container (100svh vertical scroll panel) = An empty panel of band width / .6 is placed and the stage is attached with position: fixed. The part does the same calculation with a sticky stage so it attaches to either window scroll or an inner scroll panel (data-fx-scroller)
